description: One row per shipment that has failed delivery at least once, holding its current state rather than its history: the counts of delivery attempts (ofd_count) and failures (ndr_count), the four milestone timestamps (pickup_time, latest_ofd_time, latest_ndr_time, delivery_time), and the latest reason and status. A shipment enters this table on its first failed delivery and its single row is updated as the courier retries, so the individual attempts are not visible here — only the latest one and a running count. Use it for how many shipments failed, why, and whether they were eventually delivered or returned.

columns.description: A unique identifier for the shipment record. NULL for about 10% of rows — use awb_no to identify a shipment.
An identifier for the group to which the seller belongs.
An identifier used when multiple sellers' shipments are clubbed together for logistics purposes.

The Air Waybill number, the courier's tracking number for the shipment. Effectively one row per AWB (99.7%), but a shipment handled under more than one seller_group_id is repeated, so COUNT(DISTINCT awb_no) is the reliable way to count shipments rather than COUNT(*).
The current status of the order (e.g., rto_initiated, delivered, dispatched, rto_delivered, rto_acknowledged, lost).
The name of the courier company responsible for delivering the shipment.
A unique identifier for the courier company.
The method of payment for the order (cod, online, partial-cod, prepaid).
A unique identifier for the customer who placed the order.
The full name of the customer.
A unique identifier for the seller from whom the order originated.
The timestamp when the shipment was picked up from the seller.
When the most recent delivery attempt failed. Also the partition column, so it is what any date range filters on — note it moves each time the shipment fails again.
The reason given for the most recent Non-Delivery Report (e.g., customer unavailable, otp-based cancellation, rejected by customer, no attempt, address issue).
The timestamp when the shipment was last marked as 'Out For Delivery' (OFD).
The timestamp when the shipment was successfully delivered to the customer.
How many delivery attempts have failed so far — 1 on the first failure, rising with each retry (1-3 in practice). Matches the number of ndr events recorded for the shipment.
How many times the shipment has gone out for delivery. Always at least ndr_count, since every failure follows an attempt, and higher when it was sent out again after the last failure.
Actions the seller took on the shipment, comma-separated when there is more than one (e.g., reattempt_requested, rto_requested, escalated). NULL when the seller has not acted.
The current status of the Non-Delivery Report (e.g., pending, ofd, reattempt_requested, rto_requested, rto_initiated, delivered).

description: One row per action taken on a failed delivery: the automated IVR calls, SMS and WhatsApp messages ShopDeck sends the customer, the customer's own responses, and reattempt or RTO requests raised by the seller. Each row carries the ndr_count it belongs to, so actions can be grouped by which failed attempt prompted them. This is the action detail behind the per-shipment summary in the shipment NDR reports table.

columns.description: A unique identifier for each record in the table.
The Air Waybill (AWB) number, uniquely identifying a shipment.
Which failed delivery this action belongs to, 1-3 — the value of the shipment's NDR counter at the time.
What was done on the NDR (e.g., ivr_call, sms, hsm, reattempt_requested, call, rto_requested). NULL on a small share of rows.
Who performed it: shopdeck for automated outreach, customer when the recipient responded, seller when pushed from the dashboard, playbook_agent for agent-driven flows.
The timestamp when the action was performed or recorded.
Outcome of the outreach (e.g., no-answer, completed, busy, failed, positive, negative). NULL for actions that expect no response — over half the rows.
When a response came back. NULL when none was received — about 96% of rows.
General comments or additional notes related to the NDR or action.
The content of any message sent or received, such as an SMS or IVR message.
Delivery date requested for the retry. NULL unless the action scheduled one — about 95% of rows.
A boolean flag indicating if the NDR or issue has been escalated for priority handling.
A boolean flag indicating if this record represents the first response received for a particular action or NDR cycle.
Channel the action came through (e.g., ivr_call, hsm, sms, call, dashboard, system). NULL on most rows.
The timestamp when the record was initially created in the database.
The timestamp when the record was last updated.
Cumulative IVR attempts for the AWB, 1-3.
Session ID of the IVR call. NULL unless the action was an IVR call.
The timestamp when the IVR call occurred.
Language used on the IVR call — hn or en. NULL unless the action was an IVR call.
The identifier (e.g., phone number) of the caller during the IVR interaction.
The identifier of the application or system that initiated or managed the IVR call.
IVR call length in seconds, stored as a string. NULL unless the action was a connected IVR call.
Attachments on the action, as a stringified list — almost always the empty list '[]'. Note it is a Python-style repr containing ObjectId(...) and single quotes, so it is not parseable as JSON.

description: One row per customer shipment: the customer and their contact number, the seller's pickup address, and the delivery destination, keyed by AWB number. Use it to look up who an order went to and where it was shipped from and to. Note that customer_number is stored encrypted and is decrypted only on the way out, in the rows returned to you — so filtering, joining or grouping on it matches ciphertext and will not work, and selecting it under a different name (SELECT customer_number AS phone) returns it still encrypted. Select it as customer_number and do any matching on customer_id or awb_no instead.

columns.description: Identifier of the seller group (the storefront) the shipment was placed on.
The carrier's air waybill (tracking) number for the shipment.
The seller the shipment belongs to. Rows are always restricted to the calling seller on this column.
A unique identifier for the customer the shipment was sent to.

The customer's contact number. Stored encrypted and decrypted in the returned rows only, so it cannot be filtered, joined or grouped on, and must be selected under this exact name to come back readable.
Identifier of the seller's pickup address the shipment was collected from.
City of the seller's pickup address.
State of the seller's pickup address.
Postal PIN code of the seller's pickup address.
Contact phone number registered on the seller's pickup address (not the customer's number).
Postal PIN code the shipment was delivered to.
City the shipment was delivered to.
State the shipment was delivered to.
The timestamp when the row was created. This is the table's partitioning column.
The timestamp when the row was last updated.
